title: Snapshot row
description: One line of the Merkle snapshot file: the JSON object toJsonl() in src/domain/merkle.ts writes for a SnapshotEntry, with its camelCase fields renamed to snake_case (amountMinor to amount_minor, recordedAt to recorded_at). The file is one object per line, sorted by id ascending, and `datasetSha256` on a Commitment is the sha256 of those bytes. Ascending is sortEntries() in src/domain/merkle.ts: JavaScript's `<` on the id strings, which compares UTF-16 code units, not the bytes of the ids' UTF-8 encoding. The two orders agree for well-formed ids whose characters all lie at or below U+FFFF (ASCII included) and disagree where an id has a character from U+10000 up against one from U+E000 to U+FFFF: U+10000 (UTF-8 f0 90 80 80) sorts before U+FFFD (ef bf bd) here and after it byte-wise (measured 2026-10-20). A second implementation must order by UTF-16 code units to rebuild the same leaves and the same root, or the producer must keep its ids to ASCII, which nothing in the code requires. Unlike entry.json this schema allows no `x-` keys: toJsonl() writes exactly these six, so a row with a seventh is not one this package could have produced, and a reader who rebuilt the file from the parsed rows could not reproduce the digest. The leaf hash is taken over the six fields joined with U+007C (canonical() in src/domain/merkle.ts). That join is not escaped and nothing in the code refuses a '|' inside a field, so rows that differ only in where a '|' sits share a leaf (measured 2026-10-20: id 'a|b' with asset 'c', and id 'a' with asset 'b|c'). This schema does not forbid it, because the code does not.

id.description: The entry's id. Rows are sorted by it in UTF-16 code-unit order (see the schema description above), and the tree's leaves follow that order.

asset.description: The asset the entry moves, as the producer names it.

type.description: What kind of movement it was, as the producer names it.

source.description: What produced it, as the producer names it.

amount_minor.description: Signed integer in minor units, as a decimal string. Never a float, never a formatted number. The leaf hashes this string as written.

recorded_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, seconds precision, as SnapshotEntry documents it. The leaf hashes this string as written.

integerString.description: A signed integer in its one canonical decimal form: no sign on zero, no leading zeros, no plus sign, no separators, no fraction. This states what a producer must write. commit() does not check it: it sums amounts with BigInt() and hashes the raw string, so '', ' 5', '0x10', '007' and '+5' are summed as 0, 5, 16, 7 and 5 while the leaf covers the string as given, and '12.5' throws a SyntaxError (measured 2026-10-20).
